pages.title: Lasting Powers of Attorney
pages.text: Estate planning services Lasting Powers of Attorney Peace of mind for life's what-if moments. Book initial chat Call 07902 863999 A Lasting Power of Attorney is one of the most important documents you can put in place, not because you expect something to go wrong, but because life can be unpredictable. An LPA allows you to choose someone you trust to make decisions on your behalf if you are unable to. It is a simple step that can make things far easier for your family in the future. There are two types of LPA Property and Financial Affairs This allows your chosen person to help manage banking, bills, pensions, investments, property matters and everyday finances. Health and Welfare This can cover care arrangements, medical decisions, day-to-day welfare and treatment preferences where applicable. Why LPAs matter Without an LPA, your family may face delays and legal barriers when trying to help you, even in urgent situations. The right people can act quickly Your wishes remain central Loved ones feel supported rather than stuck Important decisions are easier to manage How we help We guide you through the process clearly and carefully, helping ensure everything is completed correctly and explained properly. pages.text: Plain-English glossary Glossary of Terms Understand common estate planning words with confidence. Book initial chat Call 07902 863999 Estate planning can involve language that feels unfamiliar, but understanding the basics makes the whole process easier. This glossary explains common terms related to Wills, Trusts, Lasting Powers of Attorney, Probate and Inheritance Tax Planning. Common terms Will A legal document that sets out who should receive your estate and who should manage it after you die. Executor The person or people you appoint in your Will to carry out your wishes and administer your estate. Beneficiary A person, charity or organisation who receives something from your estate. Trust A legal arrangement where assets are held and managed by Trustees for the benefit of others. Trustee A person or professional appointed to manage Trust assets responsibly and in line with the Trust terms. Lasting Power of Attorney A document that lets you appoint trusted people to make decisions for you if you cannot make them yourself. Probate The legal and administrative process of dealing with someone's estate after they have died. Inheritance Tax A tax that may apply to an estate depending on its value, available allowances, reliefs and exemptions. Rules of Intestacy The legal rules that decide who inherits if someone dies without a valid Will. We explain things properly You do not need to know the right legal words before you speak to us. pages.text: Helpful answers Frequently Asked Questions Clear answers to the questions families often ask first. Book initial chat Call 07902 863999 Estate planning can feel full of unfamiliar words and decisions, but most questions have straightforward answers once they are explained properly. Here are some of the things families often ask us about Wills, Trusts, Probate, LPAs and tax planning. Wills and Probate Do I need a Will? A properly prepared Will helps ensure your wishes are followed, your beneficiaries are protected, children or dependants can be cared for, and confusion or disputes are less likely. What happens without a Will? If someone dies without a valid Will, their estate is distributed according to the Rules of Intestacy, which may not reflect what they would have wanted. Can I change my Will? Yes. You can update your Will when you need to, especially after major life changes such as marriage, divorce, children, moving house or bereavement. What is Probate? Probate is the legal process of managing someone's estate after they pass away. Whether it is required depends on the size and type of assets involved. LPAs, Trusts and tax planning What is a Lasting Power of Attorney? An LPA lets you appoint someone you trust to make decisions on your behalf if you are unable to. There are two types: Property and Financial Affairs, and Health and Welfare. Do I need an LPA? Having an LPA in place can prevent delays and stress for loved ones, and helps ensure the right people can step in quickly if needed. What is a Trust? A Trust is a legal arrangement used to protect or manage assets for someone else. It can help with inheritance, asset protection and vulnerable beneficiaries. Do I need a Trust? Not everyone needs a Trust. We can explain clearly whether one may be helpful for your circumstances. What is Inheritance Tax? Inheritance Tax may be payable depending on the value of an estate, allowances, reliefs and exemptions. Can I reduce inheritance tax? We can help you understand your position and explore appropriate ways of mitigating tax where possible. Why choose Pathway Estate Planning? siteGraph.summary: Estate planning services Lasting Powers of Attorney Peace of mind for life's what-if moments.
siteGraph.text: Estate planning services Lasting Powers of Attorney Peace of mind for life's what-if moments. Book initial chat Call 07902 863999 A Lasting Power of Attorney is one of the most important documents you can put in place, not because you expect something to go wrong, but because life can be unpredictable. An LPA allows you to choose someone you trust to make decisions on your behalf if you are unable to. It is a simple step that can make things far easier for your family in the future. There are two types of LPA Property and Financial Affairs This allows your chosen person to help manage banking, bills, pensions, investments, property matters and everyday finances. Health and Welfare This can cover care arrangements, medical decisions, day-to-day welfare and treatment preferences where applicable. Why LPAs matter Without an LPA, your family may face delays and legal barriers when trying to help you, even in urgent situations. The right people can act quickly Your wishes remain central Loved ones feel supported rather than stuck Important decisions are easier to manage How we help We guide you through the process clearly and carefully, helping ensure everything is completed correctly and explained properly. Book initial chat Call 07902 863999 Many people delay estate planning because it feels daunting, or because they are not sure where to start. But putting the right plan in place can make a world of difference, for you and for the people you care about. Estate planning is about more than writing a Will. It is about making sure your wishes are respected, your loved ones are supported, your estate is handled properly, and things are easier during a difficult time. At Pathway Estate Planning, we offer clear, step-by-step guidance to help you feel confident that everything is in order. Your wishes are respected Your loved ones are supported Your estate is handled properly Things are easier during a difficult time Why it matters Your Will is one of the most important documents you will ever create, but it is often easier than people expect. Some people assume estate planning is expensive or complicated. Others believe their estate will automatically pass to their spouse or family. In reality, every situation is different, and small misunderstandings can lead to serious consequences later on. Without a valid Will, your estate may be distributed under the Rules of Intestacy, which may not reflect your wishes. Lasting Powers of Attorney LPAs allow you to appoint someone you trust to make decisions for you if you ever cannot. Book initial chat Call 07902 863999 Estate planning can involve language that feels unfamiliar, but understanding the basics makes the whole process easier. This glossary explains common terms related to Wills, Trusts, Lasting Powers of Attorney, Probate and Inheritance Tax Planning. Common terms Will A legal document that sets out who should receive your estate and who should manage it after you die. Executor The person or people you appoint in your Will to carry out your wishes and administer your estate. Beneficiary A person, charity or organisation who receives something from your estate. Trust A legal arrangement where assets are held and managed by Trustees for the benefit of others. Trustee A person or professional appointed to manage Trust assets responsibly and in line with the Trust terms. Lasting Power of Attorney A document that lets you appoint trusted people to make decisions for you if you cannot make them yourself. Probate The legal and administrative process of dealing with someone's estate after they have died. Inheritance Tax A tax that may apply to an estate depending on its value, available allowances, reliefs and exemptions. Rules of Intestacy The legal rules that decide who inherits if someone dies without a valid Will. We explain things properly You do not need to know the right legal words before you speak to us. Book initial chat Call 07902 863999 Estate planning can feel full of unfamiliar words and decisions, but most questions have straightforward answers once they are explained properly. Here are some of the things families often ask us about Wills, Trusts, Probate, LPAs and tax planning. Wills and Probate Do I need a Will? A properly prepared Will helps ensure your wishes are followed, your beneficiaries are protected, children or dependants can be cared for, and confusion or disputes are less likely. What happens without a Will? If someone dies without a valid Will, their estate is distributed according to the Rules of Intestacy, which may not reflect what they would have wanted. Can I change my Will? Yes. You can update your Will when you need to, especially after major life changes such as marriage, divorce, children, moving house or bereavement. What is Probate? Probate is the legal process of managing someone's estate after they pass away. Whether it is required depends on the size and type of assets involved. LPAs, Trusts and tax planning What is a Lasting Power of Attorney? An LPA lets you appoint someone you trust to make decisions on your behalf if you are unable to. There are two types: Property and Financial Affairs, and Health and Welfare. Do I need an LPA? Having an LPA in place can prevent delays and stress for loved ones, and helps ensure the right people can step in quickly if needed. What is a Trust? A Trust is a legal arrangement used to protect or manage assets for someone else. It can help with inheritance, asset protection and vulnerable beneficiaries. Do I need a Trust? Not everyone needs a Trust. We can explain clearly whether one may be helpful for your circumstances. What is Inheritance Tax? Inheritance Tax may be payable depending on the value of an estate, allowances, reliefs and exemptions. Can I reduce inheritance tax? We can help you understand your position and explore appropriate ways of mitigating tax where possible. Why choose Pathway Estate Planning? glossary.description: A legal document that sets out who should receive your estate and who should manage it after you die.
A legal arrangement where assets are held and managed by trustees for beneficiaries.
A person or professional appointed to manage trust assets responsibly.
The person or people appointed in a Will to carry out wishes and administer an estate.
A person, charity or organisation who receives something from an estate or trust.
A document that appoints trusted people to make decisions if someone cannot make them themselves.
The legal and administrative process of dealing with someone's estate after they have died.
A tax that may apply to an estate depending on value, allowances, reliefs and exemptions.
The legal rules that decide who inherits if someone dies without a valid Will.
Planning ahead for later-life care decisions, family roles and practical options.
Exploring appropriate planning options that may reduce unnecessary tax exposure.

guardrails: Never provide definitive legal, tax, financial, probate, or care funding advice.
